raw_response:
I'm 51, been farming these 5 mu in Quzhou for 30 years. Middle school education, so I can read the extension leaflets, but honestly I trust what I see in my own fields more than what some paper says. My wife and I are the only ones at home now — the kids work in Shijiazhuang. We both take factory jobs when we can, so labor is tight. I can't be out here every day.

My land is split: 3 mu of cotton for cash, 2 mu of wheat then maize right after. That's what I've always done. Cotton pays better but it's expensive to grow — seed, pesticide, picking labor. Wheat-maize is my insurance, keeps us fed.

For the wheat, I planted it last October. Right now it's jointing, and I just put down the spring topdress — about 10 kg of urea per mu. The extension fellow said 15 kg, but fertilizer is 2.6 yuan a kilo this year and I need money for cotton seed. I'll irrigate twice more: once now at jointing, and once at heading if it doesn't rain. Last year I got 380 kg per mu, hoping for the same. I'll spray for weeds and maybe fungus if it turns wet.

Cotton goes in mid-April. I buy the hybrid seed from the county dealer, 50 yuan per mu. Before planting I plow and put down base fertilizer — about 15 kg of compound fertilizer per mu, that's roughly 5 kg of N. When it flowers in July I'll topdress another 8 kg of urea per mu. Cotton needs spraying — bollworms, aphids, always something. That's 100 yuan per mu easy. I'll irrigate twice: after planting if it's dry, and when bolls are forming. Picking is the hard part. Me and my wife will do most of it, but I might hire two people for a few days if we're behind. Hoping for 250 kg per mu of seed cotton.

Maize gets planted right after wheat harvest in early June — no time to waste, sometimes only 5 days between crops. I hire Old Wang's direct seeder, 30 yuan per mu. Fertilizer all goes down at planting: 12 kg N per mu as compound and urea. If July is dry I'll water once, but usually the summer rains are enough. Should get 400 kg per mu.

Total input cost will be around 2,200 yuan. That's a big chunk for us, but we've got to do it. My strategy is: don't change what works, spend where it matters, and always keep some cash in hand. I'd rather apply a bit more fertilizer than risk a bad year — losing 100 kg of yield hurts more than saving 50 yuan on urea.
